summary: VLM judges rendered framework output vs the brief — the consistent!=correct gate

result.task: Visual QA of LEFT column ("WITH framework") — 5 Pro pricing cards by 5 independent agents
issues: All 5 cards contain every brief element (Most popular pill, Pro tier name, description, large $29 with /mo, 3 feature lines, full-width Choose Pro CTA, elevated white surface), so the brief is satisfied.

Feature-line treatment is inconsistent across agents: agents 1 and 2 render features with a checkmark icon and dark near-black text; agents 3, 4, and 5 drop the checkmark entirely and use lighter gray text with looser line spacing. This is the biggest consistency break and makes 3 of 5 cards read as plain text rather than a feature/check list.
Feature ordering varies: agents 1, 2 list 'Unlimited projects / Priority support / Advanced analytics' while agents 3, 4, 5 list 'Unlimited projects / Advanced analytics / Priority support'.
Description copy differs between agents: 'scale your team' (agent 1), 'scale your work' (agent 2), 'ship faster' (agents 3/4/5) — minor, agent-authored, but not identical.
Checkless gray feature text on agents 3/4/5 is slightly lower contrast than the dark text on agents 1/2, though still legible.

Consistent and correct across all 5: pale-blue rounded 'Most popular' pill with blue text, bold 'Pro' heading, large bold '$29' with small gray baseline-aligned '/mo', full-width royal-blue 'Choose Pro' CTA with centered white label, and elevated white card surface with subtle shadow/border on gray background.
No broken layouts, clipping, overflow, or misalignment detected; pill, price, and CTA are visually tight and near-identical across cards.

result.task: Visual QA of the LEFT column ("WITH framework") — 5 Pro pricing cards built by 5 independent agents, judged against the brief (Most popular pill, tier name, description, large $29 price with /mo, feature lines, full-width primary CTA, elevated surface).
issues: Feature-line checkmarks are inconsistent across agents: agents 1 and 2 render a check icon before each feature line, but agents 3, 4, and 5 show plain text with NO check icons. 2 of 5 cards have the icon affordance, 3 do not.
Feature ORDER drifts: agents 1 & 2 list Unlimited projects / Priority support / Advanced analytics, while agents 3, 4 & 5 list Unlimited projects / Advanced analytics / Priority support.

Feature-line vertical spacing differs: the checkmark cards (agents 1-2) use tighter line spacing; the no-icon cards (agents 3-5) use noticeably looser gaps between feature rows, so the lists do not visually match.
Description copy varies across supposedly-identical agents ('scale your team' vs 'scale your work' vs 'ship faster'), an unintended content inconsistency.
Agent 5's card sits alone on a third row, breaking the 2-column grid rhythm and looking slightly orphaned.

Feature lines on the no-icon cards (3-5) read as lower-affordance/medium-gray body text rather than clear benefit bullets; without the check glyph they lose the 'included feature' signal the brief implied.

result.task: Visual QA of LEFT column ("WITH framework") — 5 stat cards built by 5 independent agents, against brief: 'Monthly revenue' caption, large '$48.2k', success '+12.5%' badge, on a surface.
issues: Caption color is inconsistent across agents: agents 1/3/5 use a darker slate gray (rgb 94,102,117) for 'Monthly revenue', while agents 2/4 use a lighter gray (rgb 151,161,178). The lighter variant is a visible mismatch when scanning the column.

The lighter caption on agents 2 and 4 (rgb 151,161,178 on white) is borderline low-contrast for a label — it reads notably weaker than the same caption on cards 1/3/5 and dips toward sub-AA territory for small text.

Everything else is pixel-consistent: value '$48.2k' is identical near-black (rgb 23,27,35) on all 5; badges are identical light-green pills with green '+12.5%' text (same 55px width, same left edge x=79, same bg rgb ~230,246,238); left-alignment of caption/value/badge, card width, border, corner radius and padding all match across the 5 cards.
Minor: vertical card-to-card spacing and the 'agent N' labels are uniform; no broken/misaligned elements, no overflow, no arrow-icon inconsistency in badges (none use arrows, consistently).

result.task: Visual QA of the LEFT column ("WITH framework") — 5 stat cards built by 5 independent agents, against the brief: 'Monthly revenue' caption, large '$48.2k', a success '+12.5%' badge, on a surface.
issues: All 5 cards are essentially pixel-identical: same white card surface, rounded corners, subtle border, left-aligned content, and identical padding/spacing rhythm. Excellent cross-agent convergence.
Every card contains all four required elements: 'Monthly revenue' caption (muted gray, top-left), large bold '$48.2k' value, and a green '+12.5%' success badge on a pale-green pill, on a surface.

Success badge is the most minimal valid reading of the brief: it conveys success only via green text/pill + the '+' sign, with NO up-arrow / trend glyph. The Baseline column cards both include an arrow, so the framework cards arguably under-signal 'success' relative to a richer interpretation.
Badge contrast is adequate but on the softer side — medium-green text (~#3a8f63) on a very pale mint pill. Legible at this size but borderline for small-text WCAG; could be slightly punchier.

Caption 'Monthly revenue' is sentence case here, whereas the right/baseline column shows an uppercase variant — confirms the framework enforced a single casing convention (good), but worth noting it is the lower-emphasis treatment.
No visual breakage, misalignment, overflow, or clipping detected in any of the 5 cards. Vertical baseline alignment of caption / value / badge is consistent across all instances.
Cards are slightly content-light / airy: a fair amount of empty space to the right of the value and below the badge, so the composition reads a touch sparse, but nothing off-brief.

result.task: Visual QA of LEFT column ("WITH framework") — 5 settings-row cards built by 5 independent agents. Brief: 'Push notifications' label + helper line on the left, toggle switch (on) right-aligned, comfortable padding, on a surface.
issues: CRITICAL / off-brief: the toggle is NOT right-aligned in any of the 5 cards. It sits immediately to the right of the label text (center-left of the card), leaving roughly the entire right half of every card as dead whitespace. The brief explicitly required a 'right-aligned' toggle. Notably the Baseline (right) column does push the toggle to the card's right edge correctly — so the framework cards converged on a layout that misses the single most specific spatial instruction.
Because all 5 agents converged on the same layout, they all reproduce the same right-alignment error identically — high consistency masking a shared off-brief mistake.
Label + helper text, on-toggle, comfortable padding, and the white-card-on-gray-panel surface are all present and correct in every card.
Minor: in the on state the white knob sits very tight against the inner right edge of the track, looking slightly cramped at high zoom, though acceptable at normal scale.
Layout reads as 'label + toggle hugging the text' rather than a true two-end (space-between) settings row, which is the conventional and expected pattern for this brief.

result.task: Visual QA of LEFT column ("WITH framework") — 5 settings-row cards built by 5 independent agents. Brief: 'Push notifications' label + helper line on the left, a toggle switch (on) right-aligned, comfortable padding, on a surface.
issues: Toggle is NOT right-aligned in any of the 5 cards — the core brief requirement is missed. The toggle sits immediately to the right of the label (roughly left-of-center) with a large empty gap stretching to the card's right edge. A correct settings row uses space-between so the toggle hugs the right edge (as the Baseline/right column actually does). All 5 framework agents converged on the same wrong layout.
Because the toggle floats mid-row, the rows read as unbalanced/unfinished — the wide dead space on the right makes each card look broken rather than like a real settings list item.

The label+helper text block and the toggle are not vertically center-aligned to each other in a way that reads intentional; the toggle is roughly centered against the two-line text but its left-shifted horizontal position is the dominant problem.

Consistency is near-perfect (effectively pixel-identical surface, radius, padding, type scale, toggle size/color, card height), but this high consistency just means all 5 agents reproduced the SAME layout error — consistency does not equal correctness here.

Positive: each card has a clean white surface, comfortable padding, correct text hierarchy (bold label + muted gray helper), and the toggle is correctly in the ON state (blue track, knob to the right) with adequate contrast. The only material defect is alignment/off-brief positioning.
